name: MCP23017-E_SO
title: 16-bit I/O expander with I2C (MCP23017) or SPI (MCP23S17) interface
summary: The MCP23017 and MCP23S17 add sixteen general-purpose I/O lines, in two 8-bit ports, to a host over I2C (up to 1.7 MHz) or SPI (up to 10 MHz). Each pin can be an input or output, with optional inversion, a 100 kΩ pull-up and interrupt-on-change against its last level or a set default; two interrupt outputs report the ports separately or together. Three address pins let eight devices share a bus. The part runs from 1.8 V to 5.5 V and is offered from -40 °C to +125 °C in 28-pin QFN, SOIC, SPDIP and SSOP.
key_figures: I2C 100 kHz / 400 kHz / 1.7 MHz (MCP23017); SPI 10 MHz max (MCP23S17)

notes: Order code: device, optional T for tape and reel (blank is tube), temperature E, package ML, SO, SP or SS, optional VAO for AEC-Q100 automotive qualification.
Both devices have the same pinout apart from pins 11, 13 and 14 (QFN 7, 9 and 10). On the MCP23017, GPA7 and GPB7 are outputs only.

operation.text: The MCP23017 talks I2C and the MCP23S17 talks SPI; everything else is shared. Sixteen port pins make up two 8-bit ports, A and B. Each pin has a direction bit, an input inversion bit, a weak pull-up bit and interrupt-on-change controls. There are 22 register addresses (11 A/B pairs, with IOCON appearing at two addresses), all readable by the host.

An internal POR keeps the device reset until VDD has risen far enough, then loads every register with its default (all pins inputs) and starts the state machine. VDD has to rise at 0.05 V/ms or faster to be sure of a POR. Supply, temperature and bus frequency must already be within limits when the device leaves reset.
Holding RESET low for at least 1 µs resets the device; outputs go high impedance within 1 µs of RESET falling. RESET is a Schmitt input and must be biased externally.

IOCON.BANK chooses the map. BANK = 0 (default) interleaves the A and B registers from 00h to 15h; BANK = 1 puts port A at 00h to 0Ah and port B at 10h to 1Ah. The new map takes effect as soon as the byte setting BANK is clocked in, so with auto-increment on the pointer can land on an address that no longer exists: writing 80h to IOCON at 0Ah leaves the pointer at 0Bh, which is invalid with BANK = 1. Changing BANK is best done with a single-byte write.

With IOCON.SEQOP = 0 (default) the address pointer steps after each byte and wraps to 00h past the last register. With SEQOP = 1 it stays put, so extra clocks keep reading or writing one register, handy for polling GPIO or streaming to the latches. In byte mode with BANK = 0 the pointer flips between the two registers of an A/B pair, for example between GPIOA and GPIOB, starting from either one. These modes are independent of whether the host does single or continuous transfers on the bus.

A write is: Start, control byte with R/W = 0, register address, then one or more data bytes, each acknowledged by the MCP23017, ended by Stop or Restart. Each byte is written when it is complete; a byte cut off by Stop or Restart is discarded. A read sends the register address in a write, then a Restart and the control byte with R/W = 1; the device returns the register contents until the host ends with Stop or Restart. Bus speeds are 100 kHz, 400 kHz and 1.7 MHz; 400 kHz needs VDD of 2.7 V or more and 1.7 MHz needs 4.5 V or more. At 1.7 MHz the input spike filter is off.

CS falling starts a transfer. The host sends the opcode (client address with R/W), then a register address, then writes at least one byte or clocks at least one byte out. More clocks continue to the next register as set by SEQOP; CS rising ends the transfer. The pointer wraps to zero past the last register. SPI modes 0,0 and 1,1 are supported, up to 10 MHz at 2.7 V and above and 5 MHz down to 1.8 V. In mode 1,1, CS must be toggled once after power-up before the first transfer.

The control byte is 0 1 0 0 A2 A1 A0 R/W: four fixed bits, three bits matched against the A2, A1 and A0 pins, then read (1) or write (0). Up to eight devices share one bus. The MCP23017 always compares the address pins. The MCP23S17 compares them only when IOCON.HAEN = 1; with HAEN = 0 it answers as A2 = A1 = A0 = 0. The address pins must be tied high or low in every case, HAEN set or not.

Reading GPIO returns the pin levels; reading OLAT returns the latch. Writing either register writes the latch, which drives the pins set as outputs. A pin set as input has its driver off (high impedance). GPPU switches a 100 kΩ pull-up onto pins set as inputs (40 µA to 115 µA at 5 V into a grounded pin). On the MCP23017, GPA7 and GPB7 work only as outputs and their IODIR bits must be cleared over I2C.

Only pins that are inputs and enabled in GPINTEN can interrupt; outputs never affect INT. INTCON picks the comparison per pin: against its previous value (INTCON bit 0) or against its DEFVAL bit (INTCON bit 1). The first event copies the port into INTCAP and flags the pin in INTF; further events cannot raise a new interrupt until the host clears it by reading GPIO or INTCAP, which happens once the last bit of that read is clocked out. Writing those registers does not clear it. In previous-value mode the reference becomes the level read when the interrupt clears. In DEFVAL mode the interrupt stays active as long as the pin differs from DEFVAL, whatever is read. A GPIO read while another change is pending clears and immediately re-arms the interrupt, overwriting INTCAP and losing the value it held.

By default INTA reports port A and INTB reports port B, each cleared by reading its own port's GPIO or INTCAP. With IOCON.MIRROR = 1 the two internal signals are ORed and both pins assert together; an interrupt is then cleared only by reading the port that caused it. The pins are push-pull, active-low (INTPOL = 0) or active-high (INTPOL = 1), or open-drain when ODR = 1, which overrides INTPOL.
With IOCON.DISSLW = 0 (default) the falling edge on SDA is slew-rate limited; setting DISSLW turns that off.

Operating voltage is 1.8 V to 5.5 V at -40 °C to +85 °C, 2.7 V to 5.5 V at -40 °C to +85 °C, and 4.5 V to 5.5 V at -40 °C to +125 °C. Every part is offered in the E range, -40 °C to +125 °C. VAO-suffix parts are AEC-Q100 qualified.
Pad 29 under the QFN is a thermal pad. Connect it to VSS or leave it unconnected.
